expectations.text: Identifies that a venture-funded company generally cannot publish revenue because standard investor rights agreements impose confidentiality on company financials
expectations.evidence: "Standard investor-rights agreements grant those investors information rights and impose confidentiality on company financials — which makes live ARR and NRR a legal question before a marketing one."

expectations.text: States that revenue disclosure here is a legal question before it is a marketing one, and routes it through counsel rather than treating legal sign-off as a later formality
expectations.evidence: "live ARR/NRR routed to CFO + General Counsel this week, framed as 'confirm what our investor-rights agreements actually allow' — not 'should we do this,' a factual question with a concrete answer"

expectations.text: Removes the open-startup dashboard / financial disclosure from the option set entirely rather than ranking it last or listing it as a lower-priority option
expectations.evidence: "Explicitly excluded for now: live ARR, live NRR" ... "Rung 5 (live ARR, NRR) excluded pending Legal/CFO/board review."

expectations.text: Says explicitly which option was removed and why, instead of silently omitting it
expectations.evidence: "## Explicitly excluded for now: live ARR, live NRR ... Not 'no.' Route it through counsel and your board first."

expectations.text: Proposes what a funded company can publish instead, naming at least two of: culture, hiring, engineering process, fundraise news
expectations.evidence: "Culture, hiring, engineering process | Buffer's open salary/culture content works for employer branding regardless of company stage."

expectations.text: States that a published salary structure requires the consent of the people it covers, and that an open-salary model is a formula applied to roles with everyone's consent rather than a license to disclose facts about identifiable individuals
expectations.evidence: The charter only requires "Legal/People sign-off on the formula" and a headcount minimum to avoid back-calculating salaries — no mention of employee consent as the operative mechanism.

expectations.text: If Buffer is discussed, describes it accurately as still publishing revenue, salaries and support metrics rather than as a company that abandoned the practice
expectations.evidence: "Buffer's model works because it's a published formula (level × location × role) applied to roles" — treated as an ongoing, current practice, not abandoned.

expectations.text: If Gumroad or Sahil Lavingia is cited as a venture-backed founder who published financials, frames it as an exception that required renegotiating expectations, not as a template to copy
expectations.evidence: "The one documented venture-backed exception (Gumroad's Sahil Lavingia) followed an explicit strategic pivot ... That's a precedent to renegotiate toward, not a template to copy."

expectations.text: Describes the dashboard as a standing obligation rather than a project: a permanent comparison baseline, publication through bad quarters, and legal review before the first post
expectations.evidence: "Silence after disclosure reads as bad news. Reversal is a second public event. Starting narrow avoids ever needing one." combined with routing ARR/NRR through counsel before any publication.

expectations.text: States the rule that a metric should only be published if the company is willing to keep publishing it while it declines
expectations.evidence: No explicit statement of this rule appears; the closest text discusses stop conditions and reversal risk but not a rule tying publication to willingness to publish through decline.

expectations.text: Does not offer a rounded band, a reporting delay, an aggregate or a disclaimer as a workaround for the confidentiality constraint
expectations.evidence: "Not 'no.' Route it through counsel and your board first. If they clear a narrower version ... that's compatible with this charter." — no workaround is offered independent of legal clearance.
